instruction: Plot a time series using a list of datetime objects.
output:
import datetime
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
dates = [datetime.date(2024, 1, d) for d in range(1, 6)]
values = [10, 12, 9, 14, 13]
plt.plot(dates, values, marker='o')
plt.title('Datetime Series')
plt.show()

instruction: Format the date axis with a month-and-day formatter.
output:
import datetime
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
dates = [datetime.date(2024, 1, d) for d in range(1, 11)]
values = list(range(10))
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(dates, values)
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter('%b %d'))
plt.show()

instruction: Set the date axis to show a tick at each month.

ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.MonthLocator())

instruction: Rotate the date tick labels on a time series plot.

instruction: Generate a date axis using matplotlib drange with a daily step.
output:
import datetime
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
dates = mdates.drange(datetime.date(2024, 1, 1), datetime.date(2024, 1, 11), datetime.timedelta(days=1))
values = list(range(len(dates)))
plt.plot(dates, values)
plt.title('Drange Dates')
plt.show()

instruction: Use an automatic date locator with a concise date formatter.
output:
import datetime
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
dates = [datetime.date(2024, m, 1) for m in range(1, 13)]
values = list(range(12))
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(dates, values)
locator = mdates.AutoDateLocator()
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(locator)
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.ConciseDateFormatter(locator))
plt.show()

instruction: Place date ticks on each Monday using a weekday locator.
output:
import datetime
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
dates = [datetime.date(2024, 1, d) for d in range(1, 22)]
values = [i % 5 + 1 for i in range(21)]
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(dates, values)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.WeekdayLocator(byweekday=mdates.MO))
plt.show()

instruction: Annotate a specific date on a time series plot.
output:
import datetime
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
dates = [datetime.date(2024, 1, d) for d in range(1, 8)]
values = [1, 3, 2, 6, 4, 5, 3]
plt.plot(dates, values, marker='o')
plt.annotate('Spike', xy=(datetime.date(2024, 1, 4), 6), xytext=(datetime.date(2024, 1, 5), 6.5), arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->'))
plt.title('Annotated Date')
plt.show()

instruction: Plot two time series on the same date axis with a legend.
output:
import datetime
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
dates = [datetime.date(2024, 1, d) for d in range(1, 6)]
plt.plot(dates, [10, 12, 11, 13, 15], label='A')
plt.plot(dates, [8, 9, 12, 10, 14], label='B')
plt.legend()
plt.title('Two Series')
plt.show()

instruction: Plot hourly data and place a tick at each hour.
output:
import datetime
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
start = datetime.datetime(2024, 1, 1, 0, 0)
dates = [start + datetime.timedelta(hours=h) for h in range(12)]
values = [h % 5 for h in range(12)]
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(dates, values)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.HourLocator(interval=2))
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter('%H:%M'))
plt.show()

instruction: Fill the area under a time series between the axis and the line.
output:
import datetime
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

values = [4, 6, 5, 8, 7, 9]

instruction: Add both major monthly and minor weekly date locators.
output:
import datetime
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
dates = [datetime.date(2024, 1, 1) + datetime.timedelta(days=i) for i in range(60)]
values = [i % 7 for i in range(60)]
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(dates, values)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.MonthLocator())
ax.xaxis.set_minor_locator(mdates.WeekdayLocator(byweekday=mdates.MO))
plt.show()
